does-he-love-me.title: What Are You Really Asking?
does-he-love-me.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A personalized read of what the pattern may suggest — what it says, what it doesn’t, and what to watch next. No score, no verdict, no signup.
does-he-love-me.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It works outward from you — your situation, what changed, what you actually want to know — and ends on the step that fits.

questions.q: What’s your relationship with him right now?
questions.hint: This matters more than it sounds — the same behavior means different things in different situations.

questions.q: What made you start wondering whether he loves you?
How would you describe his communication with you?
When it comes to keeping the connection going, who usually takes the lead?
What usually happens when you give him a little space?
questions.hint: Distance is one of the clearer tests of a connection — not the only one, but a real one.

questions.q: How closely do his actions match what he tells you?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest with this one — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: Steady engagement, effort from both sides, words and actions that track.
patternDetails.dontTell: Consistency shows investment — it can’t read his mind. Some people stay present for years without wanting the same future you want; consistency alone doesn’t tell you which kind of person you’re with. That part only a direct conversation can answer.

patternDetails.summary: The connection is visible; the direction isn’t.
patternDetails.dontTell: Connection and intention are different things. He can feel genuinely close and still be unsure about committing — or be ready to commit and bad at showing it. Your answers can’t separate those two. Only he can.

patternDetails.summary: Enough connection to continue; not enough consistency to rest.
patternDetails.dontTell: Mixed behavior has many possible causes: ambivalence, stress, avoidance, another priority, or a communication style that simply runs in waves. The pattern can’t tell you which one it is — and it can’t tell you what he feels, only how the connection behaves.

patternDetails.summary: The connection runs on your effort.
patternDetails.dontTell: One-sided effort doesn’t prove he doesn’t love you — some people only engage under structure, and some are simply passive. But it doesn’t prove he does, either. The honest signal here isn’t about his feelings. It’s about the shape you’re maintaining, and what it costs you.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too close, to read — which is information too.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unclear pattern isn’t a negative one. It means the data isn’t in yet. At this stage, hunting for one more “sign” tends to produce noise — every small gesture gets recruited as evidence for whichever answer you’re already leaning toward.

does-he-think-about-me.title: Why Is This on Your Mind?
does-he-think-about-me.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A read of what the pattern of contact and recall may suggest — and where it stops. No score, no verdict, no signup.
does-he-think-about-me.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. Start with why it keeps pulling at you — then read how the connection actually behaves, and end on the step that fits.

questions.q: What’s your relationship with him right now?
questions.hint: This matters more than it sounds — the same behavior means different things in different situations.

questions.q: What made you start wondering whether he thinks about you?
How would you describe his contact with you when you’re apart?
When it comes to reaching out across the distance, who usually takes the lead?
What usually happens when you don’t reach out for a while?
questions.hint: Distance is one of the clearer tests of mental engagement — not the only one, but a real one.

questions.q: How closely does what he does match what he says about thinking of you?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest with this one — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: He initiates contact unprompted, recalls what you share, and bridges the gaps.
patternDetails.dontTell: Unprompted reaching shows mental engagement; it can’t prove the nature of the thoughts. He can think about you often without it being romantic, or rarely without it meaning less when he does. The frequency of contact and the frequency of thought are only loosely coupled.

patternDetails.summary: You surface in his mind in specific contexts — songs, places, things you said.
patternDetails.dontTell: Contextual recall shows you’re in his memory; it can’t prove how often you’re in his thoughts between those moments. Memory of what you said and sustained thinking about you are different systems — both are real, neither proves the other.

patternDetails.summary: The connection lives mainly in scheduled or prompted exchanges.
patternDetails.dontTell: A gap-dependent pattern has many explanations: busyness, a different communication style, an avoidant attachment pattern, or simply a connection that hasn’t deepened enough yet. The pattern can’t tell you which — only he can.

patternDetails.summary: The reaching runs mostly from your side.
patternDetails.dontTell: One-sided reaching doesn’t prove he doesn’t think about you — some people think constantly and never reach out, especially those with avoidant attachment. But it does mean the observable evidence is thin, and that’s worth being honest about.

patternDetails.summary: Not enough behavioral evidence to read yet.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unclear pattern isn’t a negative one. At this stage, hunting for one more “sign” tends to produce noise — every small gesture gets recruited as evidence for whichever answer you’re already leaning toward.

does-my-crush-like-me-back.title: What Do You Want to Happen Next?
does-my-crush-like-me-back.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A read of what the signals available so far may honestly suggest — and where they stop. No score, no verdict, no signup.
does-my-crush-like-me-back.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. Get clear on what you want to happen next — then see what the signals so far add up to, and the move worth considering.

questions.q: What’s your situation with him right now?
questions.hint: This matters more than it sounds — early signals mean something different in week one than month three.

questions.q: What made you start wondering whether he likes you back?
How would you describe his communication with you?
When it comes to initiating contact or plans, who usually takes the lead?
What usually happens when you create a small opening — a question, an invitation, a natural pause?
questions.hint: Response to natural openings is often more diagnostic than any passively observed signal.

questions.q: How does his behavior with you compare to how he is with others?
questions.hint: This is the most diagnostic single observation in early dynamics — it controls for his baseline.

questions.q: What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest with this one — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: His attention is specific, his initiative is sustained, and his behavior differs from how he is with others.
patternDetails.dontTell: Clear mutual signals show interest; they can’t prove intention. Someone can be genuinely interested and not ready to act on it — or ready to act and bad at showing it. The signals narrow the uncertainty; they don’t close it.

patternDetails.summary: There are real signals, but not yet enough pattern to read with confidence.
patternDetails.dontTell: Promising signals can reflect interest, warmth, or simple social comfort — and the interpretive pressure of having a crush makes all three look the same. The signals haven’t had enough time to separate.

patternDetails.summary: Warmth is present, but it doesn’t point anywhere specific.
patternDetails.dontTell: Friendly warmth and romantic interest produce many of the same behaviors — eye contact, laughter, engagement. The difference is specificity and initiative, not warmth itself. Without specificity, warmth can be genuine and still platonic.

patternDetails.summary: The signals conflict, or run in one direction only.
patternDetails.dontTell: Conflicting signals have many causes: ambivalence, stress, avoidance, another priority, or a communication style that runs in waves. The pattern can’t tell you which — and it can’t tell you what he feels, only how the connection behaves.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too sparse, to read — which is information too.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unclear pattern isn’t a negative one. At this stage, every small gesture gets recruited as evidence for whichever answer you’re already leaning toward. The interpretive pressure of having a crush is real — and it’s exactly what makes early signs so unreliable.

is-he-the-one.title: What Does Your Gut Already Know?
is-he-the-one.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A read of what the relationship’s behavioral material may suggest about rightness — and where it can’t answer. No score, no verdict, no signup.
is-he-the-one.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. Your gut already has a read — the check turns it into something you can look at: where it’s strong, and where it’s still open.

questions.q: What’s your relationship with him right now?
questions.hint: This matters more than it sounds — “the one” means different things in week three and year three.

questions.q: What made you start wondering whether he’s the one?
How would you describe the consistency of your connection?
When it comes to building the relationship forward, who usually takes the lead?
What usually happens when you step back and let him lead?
questions.hint: Who carries the relationship’s direction is one of the clearer tests of “the one.”

questions.q: How closely do your values, directions, and visions for life align?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest with this one — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: Consistent engagement, mutual effort, aligned values, and a direction that holds.
patternDetails.dontTell: A strong foundation shows the relationship has the material for longevity — it can’t guarantee the outcome. “The one” is a concept that blends compatibility, timing, and choice. Behavior can show the first; the other two are partly yours to decide.

patternDetails.summary: The connection is real; the long-term answer isn’t settled yet.
patternDetails.dontTell: A genuine connection with open questions is the most common state for a developing relationship. The question “is he the one” asks more of the relationship than it has yet been asked to show — and that’s information about the question’s timing, not about the relationship’s worth.

patternDetails.summary: The connection is present; the direction isn’t clear.
patternDetails.dontTell: Direction uncertainty has many causes: the relationship is still developing, one or both of you aren’t ready to commit to a direction, or the compatibility is real but the timing isn’t. The pattern can’t tell you which.

patternDetails.summary: Something deeper than behavior is keeping the question open.
patternDetails.dontTell: Identity-level hesitation — the sense that something fundamental doesn’t fit — is real and worth taking seriously. It’s also the kind of question that no framework or reading can settle. It’s a question about who you are and what you need, and it belongs to you.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too close, to read — which is information too.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unclear pattern isn’t a negative one. It means the relationship hasn’t yet produced the kind of behavioral history that “the one” question needs — across time, across contexts, across stress. That’s a timing issue, not a verdict.

does-he-miss-me.title: A Sign to Reach Out — or Let Go?
does-he-miss-me.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A read of what behavior across distance may honestly suggest — and where it stops. No score, no verdict, no signup.
does-he-miss-me.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. Name what you’re really looking for — closure, a reason to reach out, or peace with the silence — and end on the step that fits.

questions.q: What’s your situation with him right now?
questions.hint: This matters more than it sounds — absence means different things at different stages.

questions.q: What made you start wondering whether he misses you?
How would you describe his contact with you across the distance?
When it comes to bridging the distance, who usually takes the lead?
What usually happens when the distance stretches longer than usual?
questions.hint: How someone handles extended absence is one of the clearer tests of whether the distance is situational or meaningful.

questions.q: How closely does what he does across the distance match what he says about missing you?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest with this one — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: He bridges the distance unprompted, stays connected through the gap, and backs his words with action.
patternDetails.dontTell: Active reaching across distance shows the connection survives absence; it can’t prove the subjective experience of missing. He can reach back from habit, attachment, or genuine longing — behavior can’t distinguish between them. What it can show is that the distance hasn’t broken the pattern.

patternDetails.summary: The connection survives the distance, even if the reaching is quieter.
patternDetails.dontTell: Connection continuity shows the bond survives absence; it can’t prove the felt experience of missing. Some people maintain connection out of habit or attachment without the emotional pull of longing. Continuity is reassuring, but it’s not the same signal as actively reaching back.

patternDetails.summary: The connection lives mainly in prompted or scheduled contact across the distance.
patternDetails.dontTell: A gap-dependent pattern has many explanations: busyness, a different communication style, an avoidant attachment pattern, or simply a connection that hasn’t deepened enough to produce reaching across distance. The pattern can’t tell you which — and it can’t access what he privately feels.

patternDetails.summary: The distance has widened, and the reaching has thinned or stopped.
patternDetails.dontTell: Suppressed behavior across distance has two very different possible causes: he doesn’t miss you, or he does but suppresses the reaching (avoidant attachment, stress, self-protection). The pattern can’t distinguish between them — only a direct conversation or more time can. What it can tell you is that the observable evidence is thin.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too close, to read — which is information too.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unclear pattern isn’t a negative one. It means the distance hasn’t yet produced the kind of behavioral record that would let you read it honestly. At this stage, hunting for one more “sign” tends to produce noise — every small gesture gets recruited as evidence.

is-he-serious-about-me.title: What Would Make You Feel Sure?
is-he-serious-about-me.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A read of what the relationship’s directional behavior may honestly suggest about intention — and where it can’t answer. No score, no verdict, no signup.
is-he-serious-about-me.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. Name what would actually settle it for you — then read which way things are moving, and end on the step that fits.

questions.q: What’s your relationship with him right now?
questions.hint: This matters more than it sounds — “serious” means different things at different stages.

questions.q: What made you start wondering whether he’s serious about you?
How would you describe the consistency of his engagement?
When it comes to building something forward, who usually takes the lead?
What usually happens when you stop pushing things forward?
questions.hint: Who carries the relationship’s direction is one of the clearer tests of intention.

questions.q: How closely do his actions match what he says about being serious?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest with this one — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: Consistent engagement, mutual forward effort, and actions that match his words.
patternDetails.dontTell: Clear behavioral intention shows the relationship is being built, not just maintained. It can’t guarantee the outcome — someone can build with genuine intention and still hit a wall, or be serious and bad at showing it. The pattern narrows the uncertainty; it doesn’t close it.

patternDetails.summary: The relationship is growing, but the direction hasn’t been named yet.
patternDetails.dontTell: Building but undefined is the most common state for a developing relationship. The “is he serious” question asks the relationship to have a definition it hasn’t yet been given — and that’s a conversation question, not a signs-reading question.

patternDetails.summary: The connection is comfortable, but it isn’t moving forward.
patternDetails.dontTell: A comfortable holding pattern can last for years. It doesn’t prove he’s not serious — some people are content and serious simultaneously. But it does mean the behavioral evidence of intention — forward motion, definition, investment in building — is absent, and that’s worth being honest about.

patternDetails.summary: The engagement thins when things deepen, and the direction stays unclear.
patternDetails.dontTell: Avoidant uncertainty has two different possible causes: he’s not as serious as you need, or he is but suppresses the forward motion (avoidant attachment, fear, timing). The pattern can’t distinguish between them — only a direct conversation or more time can. What it can tell you is that the observable evidence isn’t matching the question.

patternDetails.path: Not enough time yet to know
patternDetails.summary: Too early to read intention — which is information too.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unclear pattern isn’t a negative one. It means the relationship hasn’t yet been tested at the depth the “is he serious” question requires — across stress, across time, across the conversations that reveal direction. That’s a timing issue, not a verdict.

1111-meaning.title: Why Is 1111 on Your Mind?
1111-meaning.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A personalized read of your 1111 sightings — what it suggests, what it doesn’t, and what to watch next. No score, no verdict, no signup.
1111-meaning.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads whether visual attention-capture explains the frequency, whether meaning-making is the real gain, and whether the portal or manifestation-confirmation framing is doing work the pattern can’t support.

questions.q: What were you going through when 1111 started showing up?
questions.hint: The situation shapes how the same sightings read.

questions.q: What put the significance of 1111 in your head?
How do you make sense of seeing 1111 so often?
questions.hint: The frequency has a specific, honest explanation.

questions.q: What do you do when you see 1111?
How much do you read the sightings as a portal or awakening?
Do you read 1111 as confirming a manifestation?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: The frequency is largely visual and cultural, not supernatural.
patternDetails.dontTell: Recognizing visual attention-capture doesn’t prove 1111 has no personal meaning — the meaning-making is real and usable as reflection. What it does is name the frequency’s cause, which is attention and culture, not supernatural signaling.

patternDetails.summary: You’re using the sighting as usable reflection, not a portal.
patternDetails.dontTell: Meaning-making doesn’t prove the sighting is “the” message — it proves the reflection is the honest gain, which works whether or not 1111 is supernaturally caused.

patternDetails.summary: The portal framing is extending seeking without delivering.
patternDetails.dontTell: Portal-seeking doesn’t prove there is no portal — nothing can prove a negative on an unfalsifiable claim. What it does is name that the portal framing isn’t supported by evidence and can extend seeking without delivering.

patternDetails.summary: The confirmation-bias pattern — the sighting doesn’t confirm the outcome.
patternDetails.dontTell: Reading it as confirmation doesn’t prove your manifestation isn’t underway — the outcome may or may not be progressing on its own timeline. What it does is name that the sighting itself doesn’t confirm the outcome; it confirms that 1111 has entered your attention.

patternDetails.summary: Too new, or too close, to read honestly.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unreadable pattern isn’t a negative one — it means the data isn’t in yet. At this stage, hunting for one more sign of a portal or confirmation tends to produce noise: every neutral event gets recruited as evidence for whichever reading you’re already leaning toward.

222-meaning.title: What Are Your 222 Sightings Pointing At?
222-meaning.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A personalized read of your 222 sightings — what they suggest, what they don’t, and what to watch next. No score, no verdict, no signup.
222-meaning.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads whether attentional priming explains the frequency, whether meaning-making is the real gain, and whether message-seeking is doing anxiety work — and ends on the step that fits.

questions.q: What were you living through when 222 started showing up?
questions.hint: The context shapes how the same sightings read.

questions.q: What put the “222 means something” idea in your head?
How did the frequency of seeing 222 strike you?
questions.hint: The shape of the frequency is the clearest signal there is.

questions.q: What are you actually doing with the number?
Are you reading the sightings as confirmation of something?
How are you framing what the sightings mean?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: The frequency is attention — a documented effect, not a message.
patternDetails.dontTell: Attentional priming doesn’t prove the sightings are meaningless — the felt-significance of a pattern is genuinely yours to use. What it can’t prove is that 222 is a message directed at you: the frequency is explained by attention, which is a stronger, evidence-backed account than the supernatural one.

patternDetails.summary: You’re using 222 as reflection — which works, with or without a channel.
patternDetails.dontTell: Meaning-making doesn’t prove the reflection is “the” meaning of 222 — there is no single fixed meaning the number carries. What it can’t prove is that the insight originates externally; the value is that it surfaces something already true about you, which is enough.

patternDetails.summary: The pull is toward a decoded message the evidence doesn’t support.
patternDetails.dontTell: Message-seeking doesn’t prove the sightings are meaningless — the meaning-making is real and usable. What it can’t prove is that any reader or framework can decode a supernatural message: no one possesses that certainty, and anyone guaranteeing it is selling a confidence nobody holds.

patternDetails.path: The value-framing is doing anxiety work
patternDetails.summary: Framing 222 as a warning is extending the unease.
patternDetails.dontTell: Anxiety-amplification doesn’t prove the warning-frame is wrong about an external threat — only that the framing is the mechanism extending the distress. What it can’t prove is that 222 is a negative omen: the associations are neutral until you frame them, and the frame is yours to change.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too close, to read honestly.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unreadable pattern isn’t a negative one — it means the data isn’t in yet. At this stage, hunting for one more sign of a message tends to produce noise: every neutral event gets recruited as evidence for whichever reading you’re already leaning toward.

am-i-an-empath.title: Are You an Empath — or Is the Label Doing the Work?
am-i-an-empath.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A personalized read of whether high empathy, sensitivity, or identity-anchoring best describes your pattern — what it suggests, what it doesn’t, and what to watch next. No score, no verdict, no signup.
am-i-an-empath.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads whether you’re a high-empathy person, whether absorption is contagion or empathy, and whether the label is doing diagnostic or identity work — and ends on the step that fits.

questions.q: What brings you to this question?
questions.hint: This matters — the situation shapes how the same experience reads.

questions.q: What put the “empath” idea in your head?
When someone near you is upset, what happens in you?
questions.hint: The intensity of feeling others’ states is the clearest signal there is.

questions.q: Can you tell whose feeling you’re in?
Which best describes what you experience?
questions.hint: Empathy and sensitivity overlap but are not identical — and the distinction changes what would help.

questions.q: What is the “empath” label doing for you?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest with this one — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: The answers describe real, high affective empathy — a measurable trait, not a special status.
patternDetails.dontTell: Genuine high empathy doesn’t prove special status — the trait is a dimension of normal human variation, not a category apart. What it does confirm is that the feeling is real, which means the useful work is boundary and self-regulation, not a reading that certifies a gift.

patternDetails.summary: The trait reads more like sensory-processing sensitivity than feeling others’ emotions.
patternDetails.dontTell: Sensitivity isn’t lesser than empathy — it’s a different trait with a different prescription. What the answers don’t prove is that you lack empathy; they suggest the driver of your experience is sensory load, which is addressable on its own terms.

patternDetails.summary: Strong feeling of others’ states plus poor boundary differentiation — the depleting combination.
patternDetails.dontTell: Boundary depletion doesn’t mean you have more empathy than others — high empathy without boundary skills is its own pattern, and the boundary issue is the real, addressable thing. If the absorption is causing you distress, a licensed therapist offers more reliable support than any spiritual reading — boundary patterns respond to specific, evidence-based work.

patternDetails.path: The label is doing identity work
patternDetails.summary: The “empath” label is functioning as identity-anchoring rather than a tool to understand your pattern.
patternDetails.dontTell: Identity use of the label isn’t wrong — it can be a way to make sense of real experience. What deserves noticing is when the label becomes explanation-for-everything, because that can keep you seeking confirmation instead of engaging the trait. Anyone who certifies you as a “true empath” with a special mission is offering a projection dressed as validation.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too close, to read honestly.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unreadable pattern isn’t a negative one — it means the data isn’t in yet. At this stage, hunting for one more sign that you’re an empath tends to produce noise: every neutral event gets recruited as evidence for whichever reading you’re already leaning toward.

am-i-in-love.title: What Are You Actually Feeling?
am-i-in-love.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A personalized read of which state your experience may point to — what it suggests, what it doesn’t, and what to watch next. No score, no verdict, no signup.
am-i-in-love.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It works outward from you — how long it’s been, what the feeling looks like day to day, and what you actually want to know — and ends on the step that fits.

questions.q: How long have you been feeling this way about them?
questions.hint: This matters more than it sounds — the same intensity means different things in week two and year two.

questions.q: Where are you with them right now?
How does the feeling show up day to day?
questions.hint: Intensity is infatuation’s signature — not love’s proof. The peak feeling is most powerful precisely because it isn’t yet anchored.

questions.q: When you picture them happy, what’s your first reaction?
questions.hint: The clearest marker of love is wanting their flourishing — choosing them across inconvenience, not just feeling pulled toward them.

questions.q: Has the early intensity eased, and what happened to the care?
questions.hint: This is the one test that separates love from infatuation — but it can only be run once the flush has had time to fade.

questions.q: Does this feel different from past intense feelings?
questions.hint: Sometimes the novelty is in this person; sometimes it’s the familiarity of your own infatuation pattern. The question is partly about you.

questions.q: What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest with this one — it decides what actually helps you next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.path: Early infatuation — the flush is at its peak
patternDetails.summary: The intensity you describe is the early state — real, powerful, and exactly what infatuation looks like before it has declared its trajectory.
patternDetails.dontTell: Intensity is not a measure of love — it’s infatuation’s signature. The peak feeling is most powerful precisely because it isn’t yet anchored, and using it as proof reverses the actual signal. when-will-i-meet-my-soulmate.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A read of what the pattern of your waiting may suggest — and where it stops. No score, no verdict, no signup.
when-will-i-meet-my-soulmate.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. Start with where you are and what triggered the question — then read the shape of your waiting, and end on the step that fits.

questions.q: Where are you in life right now?
questions.hint: This shapes what the question is really doing for you.

questions.q: What brought the question up for you right now?
When you think about not having met them yet, how does it sit day to day?
questions.hint: Healthy patience lives the present; anxious waiting postpones it.

questions.q: When it hasn’t happened, where does your mind go?
questions.hint: Timing is shaped by circumstance far more than by your worth.

questions.q: Does the “soulmate” idea help you, or keep you searching?
Is there a part of this you feel you can actually affect?
questions.hint: Not the timing — but your approach to connection is in your hands.

questions.q: What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest — it decides what actually helps next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: The waiting isn’t costing you the years — you’re living the present while staying open.
patternDetails.dontTell: Healthy patience is a shape, not a guarantee. Living fully doesn’t make the partner arrive sooner — but it means the time isn’t lost, and a fuller life is what a future partnership joins rather than replaces. The quiz can’t tell you when; this pattern only tells you how you’re spending the in-between.

patternDetails.summary: The present feels suspended until the partner arrives — which extends the very loneliness it seeks to end.
patternDetails.dontTell: Anxious waiting isn’t a flaw in you and it doesn’t mean the partner won’t come. It means the shape of the wait is costing the years it spans. The quiz can’t date the meeting — but it can show this pattern, because the waiting shape is the part you can actually affect.

patternDetails.summary: The absence is reading as a verdict on your worth — the most costly pattern this question installs.
patternDetails.dontTell: Self-blame is a pattern, not a finding. Nothing in your answers tells us the absence is your fault — and reading it as one tends to narrow confidence and extend the isolation it tries to explain. The quiz can’t date the meeting; what it can do is name this pattern plainly, because naming it is the first step out of it.

patternDetails.summary: You’re wondering whether the soulmate frame is helping or just keeping you searching.
patternDetails.dontTell: Questioning the concept isn’t rejecting love or proving it false. It’s checking whether the frame fits your actual life. The quiz can’t settle whether soulmates exist — the concept is genuinely ambiguous — but it can show when the question is doing anxiety work rather than diagnostic work, and that distinction is yours to use.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too close, to read — which is information too.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unclear pattern isn’t a negative one. It means the data isn’t in yet. At this stage, hunting for one more “sign” or asking a reading to date the meeting tends to produce noise — every small thing gets recruited as evidence for whichever answer you’re already leaning toward. The forecast isn’t available, and forcing one here would be the least reliable move.

who-is-my-soulmate.title: What Is Your Search Really About?
who-is-my-soulmate.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A read of what your search may actually be about — whether you’re seeking a person or a feeling, whether the concept is doing diagnostic or anxiety work, and what to watch next. No score, no verdict, no signup.
who-is-my-soulmate.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It works outward from your situation — what you’re looking for, what the soulmate idea is doing in your search, and what fits next.

questions.q: Where are you in your search right now?
questions.hint: This shapes what the question is really doing — the same wish means different things in different places.

questions.q: What brought the question up for you?
When you picture “my soulmate,” what are you actually looking for?
questions.hint: Seeking a person and seeking a feeling are different searches with different honest trajectories.

questions.q: Is the soulmate idea helping you look, or keeping you looking?
questions.hint: The concept can do diagnostic work, or anxiety work that extends the search.

questions.q: Do you go back over past connections as maybe-the-one?
questions.hint: The retrospective check is often an anxiety pattern wearing the language of fate.

questions.q: Can you tell the early intensity from what a connection settles into?
questions.hint: Intense early recognition can mimic the signal; what it settles into is the closer test.

questions.q: What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest — it decides what would actually help next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: You describe recognition with someone now, and you can tell the early intensity from what it settles into.
patternDetails.dontTell: Recognition with a present person is real, but it can’t prove “the one” or that it will last. No framework — and no reading — can name a soulmate in advance; the recognition happens through relating, not before it.

patternDetails.summary: You’re seeking a person or a feeling, but no present connection has settled into recognition yet.
patternDetails.dontTell: A reading can’t name your soulmate in advance — anyone who claims to is offering a projection dressed as foresight. What you can do is notice unusual depth and mutual recognition as they actually appear, in real time.

patternDetails.summary: You keep returning to past connections as maybe-the-one.
patternDetails.dontTell: Revisiting the past can be genuine recognition, but more often it renews a wish without producing new understanding. A reading that predicts reunion tends to keep the question open — and keep you paying. The honest test is whether looking back produces new material or just renews the want.

patternDetails.summary: The soulmate idea may be doing anxiety work more than diagnostic work in your search.
patternDetails.dontTell: Questioning the concept isn’t the same as deciding it’s false — it’s a real, honest question. But if the search is driven by repetitive overthinking or distress that touches daily life, a licensed therapist is the more reliable form of support than any reading.

patternDetails.summary: Too uncertain, or too soon, to form a pattern — which is information too.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unclear pattern isn’t a negative one. It means the data isn’t in yet. Hunting for one more sign tends to produce noise — every small gesture gets recruited as evidence for whichever answer you’re already leaning toward.

zodiac-compatibility.title: Are You Reflecting, or Seeking a Verdict?
zodiac-compatibility.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A personalized read of how you’re using the compatibility framework — as a reflective lens or as a predictor — what it suggests, what it doesn’t, and what to watch next. No score, no verdict, no signup.
zodiac-compatibility.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads whether you’re using zodiac as meaning-making or reaching for a sign-based verdict — and ends on the step that fits.

questions.q: What kind of relationship situation are you in right now?
questions.hint: This matters — the situation shapes how the compatibility question reads.

questions.q: What put the compatibility question in your head?
Are you using the framework as reflection or seeking a prediction?
questions.hint: The honest line most people cross without noticing.

questions.q: How do you read the felt-accuracy of compatibility descriptions?
When your relationship is hard, what do you reach for?
Have you weighed connections by sign?
What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest — this decides what actually helps next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: You’re using zodiac as a reflective lens, not a verdict.
patternDetails.dontTell: Using the framework as meaning-making doesn’t prove the signs “mean” anything about your fate — nothing can prove a prediction the evidence doesn’t support. What it does is give you a real, usable lens on your dynamic, and the reflection works whether or not the prediction holds.

patternDetails.summary: You’re reaching for the framework as a predictor.
patternDetails.dontTell: Reaching for a sign verdict doesn’t make you wrong — the wish for one is human and enormous. What it does is trade a usable lens for a prediction the evidence can’t deliver, and deterministic thinking can quietly avoid the behavioral work the relationship actually needs.

patternDetails.summary: The difficulty is being read as the signs.
patternDetails.dontTell: Reading the difficulty as signs doesn’t prove the difficulty isn’t real — it proves the cause is being placed where it can’t be worked. The relationship’s fate isn’t settled by the chart; it’s built in the behavioral work the sign framing can postpone.

patternDetails.summary: The search for the right sign is doing the work.
patternDetails.dontTell: Match-seeking doesn’t prove signs never matter — they can be a pleasing lens. What it proves is that using them as a filter over behavior costs real possibilities, and no sign pairing is reliably “most compatible” in the evidence.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too close, to read honestly.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unreadable pattern isn’t a negative one — it means the data isn’t in yet. At this stage, hunting for one more sign of compatibility tends to produce noise: every neutral event gets recruited as evidence for whichever reading you’re already leaning toward.

is-he-cheating.title: Is He Cheating? What You Can and Can’t Know
is-he-cheating.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A personalized read of what your observations suggest, what they don’t prove, and what to watch next — no verdict, no signup.
is-he-cheating.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads what you’ve actually observed across four signals — his openness, his time, his warmth, and his device habits — and sorts your suspicion into one of five patterns, ending on the step that fits.

questions.q: What are you living through right now?
questions.hint: The situation shapes how the same behavior reads.

questions.q: What put the “is he cheating” question in your head?
questions.hint: A hunch, a find, and a rumor deserve different weights.

questions.q: How has his openness about his life changed?
questions.hint: Detail collapsing into vagueness — or flowing in from topics that used to be closed — is a change in the information environment.

questions.q: How has his time and routine changed?
questions.hint: An affair requires hours. Watch for unaccounted windows that repeat, and explanations that stay thin.

questions.q: How has the warmth between you changed?
questions.hint: Withdrawal that reads as exhaustion differs from withdrawal that reads as avoidance — and over-sweetness after cold stretches is its own signature.

questions.q: How have his device habits changed?
questions.hint: Affairs require a communication channel. A new boundary around the phone is the classic first flag — but privacy is a value, not a confession.

questions.q: What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest — this decides what actually helps next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: Several of his signals shifted together — information, time, warmth, devices — which is the closest thing to signal that observation offers.
patternDetails.dontTell: A cluster of changes doesn’t prove an affair — it proves something is worth a direct conversation. The honest move is the conversation stated plainly and once, not an interrogation designed to relieve anxiety, which produces denials whether or not anything happened.

patternDetails.summary: The warmth dropped, but the information and the time didn’t — which points at something internal, not a third person.
patternDetails.dontTell: Distance without concealment doesn’t prove a third person — it often points at something internal: stress, a rough season, shame about a failure you don’t know yet. The risk is answering a distance question with surveillance, which costs the trust you still have.

patternDetails.summary: One signal changed against his baseline, but the rest held — one vivid sign is noise until it develops company.
patternDetails.dontTell: One pulled thread doesn’t make a case — a single change against his baseline is Tuesday, not evidence, and three weak signs from one domain are one life change. The risk is sign-stacking: counting list items instead of weighing them, which turns noise into a verdict.

patternDetails.summary: Against his own normal, the four signals haven’t moved together — which doesn’t prove a negative, only that observation shows no cluster.
patternDetails.dontTell: A steady baseline isn’t a clean bill of conduct — it means observation shows no cluster right now, which can change. The risk is either dismissing a real slow shift or, just as wrongly, recruiting ordinary behavior as evidence because the fear is loud.

patternDetails.summary: The signals are mixed or mid-range — too early, or too close, to read honestly.
patternDetails.dontTell: A mixed read isn’t a negative one — it means the data isn’t in yet. At this stage, hunting for one more sign that he’s cheating tends to produce noise: every neutral event gets recruited as evidence for whichever reading you’re already leaning toward.

will-he-come-back.title: Will He Come Back? An Honest Pattern Check
will-he-come-back.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A personalized read of your wait — what your answers suggest, what they don’t prove, and what to look at next. No score, no verdict, no signup.
will-he-come-back.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads the shape of the ending, whether he returns after distance as a pattern, how much of your day is checking, and how the pain has been moving — and ends on the step that fits.

questions.q: Where is the connection sitting right now?
questions.hint: This shapes how the same signals read.

questions.q: What put the “will he come back” question in your head?
What shape was the ending?
questions.hint: Clean endings are easier to grieve; ambiguous ones keep the question open by design.

questions.q: After pulling away before, has he returned?
questions.hint: A pattern of return is real — and statistically tends to be a pattern of leaving, which is the part that repeats.

questions.q: How much of your day goes to checking on him?
questions.hint: His socials, the signs, mutual friends — the most measurable signal of processing versus cycling.

questions.q: Over the weeks since, how has the pain moved?
questions.hint: Processing integrates; cycling resets to peak. The course tells you which is happening.

questions.q: What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest — this decides what actually helps next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: Your answers point at the decision underneath the prediction — whether you’re asking about his behavior or quietly deferring your own.
patternDetails.dontTell: A decision question answered by waiting is a decision deferred — and the cost compounds quietly. No reading can or should make the wait-or-leave choice for you; any reader who offers to, or names a reunion with a timeline, is selling certainty nobody has.

patternDetails.summary: Your answers point at the control question — the wish that a strategy could produce another person’s choice.
patternDetails.dontTell: No strategy honestly produces another person’s decision — and the rituals or protocols that promise to (come-back spells, return-love upsells) monetize the exact promise that makes the question hold. The honest answer is that your recovery is the part you can actually do.

patternDetails.summary: Your answers point at the closure question — whether the ending was clean enough to grieve or ambiguous enough to keep the question open.
patternDetails.dontTell: An ambiguous ending keeps the question open by design — it usually means the ending wasn’t done well, not that it wasn’t done. A reading that keeps predicting reunion tends to keep you paying; a closure-framed read, focused on what the relationship was, is the honest fit.

patternDetails.summary: Your answers point at the loop — the checking and re-asking the question encourages, which deepens the very pain it tries to read.
patternDetails.dontTell: The loop isn’t a sign about him — it’s the mind re-asking the question rather than gathering new information. A reading that promises to settle it can deepen the very loop it claims to calm; if the checking is affecting your sleep, work, or daily life, a licensed therapist is the more honest match than another reading.

patternDetails.summary: Your answers point at a real pattern — he has returned after distance before, which raises the base rate modestly but says nothing about today.
patternDetails.dontTell: Past return is not prediction — it says he has returned, not that he will, and the leaving tends to repeat too. The useful question may be about the cycle itself, not the next return, and that question is often better served by therapy or honest reflection than by another reading promising a reunion.

am-i-cursed.title: Am I Cursed?
am-i-cursed.launchSub: A two-minute check on whether the bad luck is clustering in a real, addressable way — or your mind is pattern-making under strain.

questions.q: What’s the shape of what you’re living through right now?
What put the “cursed” idea in your head?
Where is the bad luck clustering?
How manageable has life felt lately?
Where did the “cursed” claim come from?
Over the last few weeks, how has the streak been moving?
What do you most want to know?
What would honestly help most?

patternDetails.summary: Your bad luck is clustering in one addressable domain — which is the honest signal to investigate it, not to curse it.
patternDetails.dontTell: A focused cluster doesn’t prove a curse — it points at a real, addressable cause worth investigating directly. A doctor, an inspection, or a hard look at the situation is the honest first match; a reader is not.

patternDetails.summary: When control feels low, the mind generates patterns — curses, signs, conspiracies — to regain a felt sense of it.
patternDetails.dontTell: A stress-driven pattern doesn’t prove there’s no real problem — it proves the attribution arrives precisely when life is hardest to verify. What it can’t prove is a directed cause: widespread misfortune under low control is the signature of strain, not malice.

patternDetails.summary: A reader who diagnoses a curse and offers to remove it for a fee has a direct financial stake in the diagnosis — the structural red flag.
patternDetails.dontTell: A reader’s curse diagnosis can’t prove a curse — the concept is unfalsifiable, and this source profits from the claim. What it can’t tell you is anything about your actual situation: walk away from any reader who offers both the diagnosis and the paid removal.

patternDetails.summary: Your bad luck is moving through a finite window — a hard season, not a permanent condition.
patternDetails.dontTell: A finite streak doesn’t prove a curse is lifting — it usually means the underlying stressor or season is passing. What it can’t prove is that worsening means a curse is strengthening: it usually means the underlying cause hasn’t been addressed yet.

patternDetails.summary: Too early, or too close, to read honestly.
patternDetails.dontTell: An unreadable pattern isn’t a negative one — it means the data isn’t in yet. At this stage, hunting for one more sign of a curse tends to produce noise: every neutral event gets recruited as evidence for whichever reading you’re already leaning toward.

will-i-get-the-job.title: Will I Get the Job?
will-i-get-the-job.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. A pattern check on what the waiting is doing to you — not a called outcome. It reads the cost of the uncertainty, your timeline realism, your fit read, and how much weight one offer is carrying — then ends on the step that fits.
will-i-get-the-job.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads how much the uncertainty is costing you, whether your timeline is realistic, how clearly you’ve read fit, and how much weight this one outcome is carrying — and ends on the step that fits.

questions.q: Where are you in the process?
questions.hint: This shapes how the same wait reads.

questions.q: What put the “will I” question in your head?
How much is the uncertainty costing you?
questions.hint: Sleep, mood, the ability to do other things.

questions.q: How does the wait feel against your timeline?
questions.hint: The planning fallacy says your estimate is probably short.

questions.q: How clearly have you read fit — for you, not for them?
questions.hint: The better question hiding behind the prediction.

questions.q: How much weight is this one outcome carrying?
questions.hint: The impact bias says we overestimate how much it’ll affect us.

questions.q: What do you most want to know?
questions.hint: Be honest — it decides what actually helps next.

questions.q: What would help you most right now?

patternDetails.summary: Your answers describe a wait running on silence more than on signal — the uncertainty is doing the work, not the process.
patternDetails.dontTell: A quiet inbox cannot tell you the outcome — silence is the default state of a process you can’t see, not evidence of rejection or selection. No honest reading can call the offer from it.

patternDetails.summary: The wait is really a decision you’re carrying — keep waiting, or run a real search.
patternDetails.dontTell: A reading can give you a richer view of each path, but the decision to keep waiting or move on stays yours — and any reader who offers to make it for you is selling certainty nobody has.

patternDetails.summary: The “will I” loop is hiding the better question — is this the right job for me?
patternDetails.dontTell: A good fit read can’t tell you whether they’ll pick you — the two questions are separate. But it can tell you whether this job is worth holding your life open for, which the prediction never could.

patternDetails.summary: The “taking too long” feeling is mostly a mismatch of expectation — not a slow process meaning rejection.
patternDetails.dontTell: A slow timeline can’t tell you the outcome — it usually means process, not rejection. Reading slowness as a verdict is the one move the evidence doesn’t support.

patternDetails.summary: This one outcome is carrying more weight than the result can bear — the impact bias at full volume.
patternDetails.dontTell: No honest reading can tell you the outcome — and betting the meaning of your whole working life on one hire is a weight the result was never built to carry. A parallel search is the more honest match than a verdict.

signs-from-deceased-loved-ones.title: What Is Your Experience Asking For?
signs-from-deceased-loved-ones.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. It maps how you interact with signs, whether the experience brings peace or sustains an anxious loop, and what kind of support fits your grief.
signs-from-deceased-loved-ones.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads whether your relationship to signs is bringing peace or sustaining an anxious loop, and matches you with a grounded next step.

questions.q: How long has it been since your loss, and how does your grief currently feel?
questions.hint: Context first — fresh loss and long-carried grief process symbolism differently.

questions.q: What kind of encounter or sign prompted this question?
questions.hint: Where the attention was caught.

questions.q: How do you usually feel in the hours after you notice a potential sign?
questions.hint: The immediate emotional wake is the clearest signal of what the perception is doing.

questions.q: How often do you find yourself actively looking or waiting for signs?
questions.hint: Spontaneous perception brings comfort; compulsive scanning produces anxiety.

questions.q: What meaning does your mind tend to attach to these moments?
questions.hint: What is the sign being asked to carry?

questions.q: How does it feel when weeks go by and you experience no signs whatsoever?
questions.hint: The quiet room reveals whether attachment security is intact.

questions.q: What are you most hoping to understand right now?
questions.hint: Your real intention decides the practice fit.

questions.q: What kind of support would honestly serve you best at this stage?
questions.hint: Different stages need different kinds of holding.

patternDetails.summary: Your encounters arrive organically and leave you with warmth, peace, and resilience.
patternDetails.dontTell: It does not prove supernatural transmission in an empirical lab — but in this pattern, scientific proof is unnecessary because the emotional comfort is self-contained and free of distress.

patternDetails.summary: Looking for signs has quietly converted from a spontaneous comfort into an exhausting anxiety loop.
patternDetails.dontTell: More signs cannot heal the underlying grief — compulsive scanning is an anxiety symptom that keeps the nervous system in suspended hyper-vigilance.

patternDetails.summary: Encounters are carrying the heavy burden of words left unsaid or caregiver regrets.
patternDetails.dontTell: No sign or external reading can absolve you — absolution must come from understanding that human relationships are imperfect, and a lifetime of love is not defined by its final difficult days.

patternDetails.summary: The silence feels like abandonment, but it is the natural fatigue of an overwhelmed nervous system.
patternDetails.dontTell: Silence does not mean absence of love — your loved one is not withholding affection; your brain is simply exhausted from processing profound loss.

patternDetails.summary: You are in between skepticism and longing, with too many mixed feelings to form a fixed pattern.
patternDetails.dontTell: You do not have to choose right now between cold materialism and total supernatural belief — you can hold an experience as meaningful without declaring it a proven miracle.

patternDetails.summary: A gentle, steady relationship with their memory that needs no dramatic external validation.
patternDetails.dontTell: You do not need to seek out dramatic mediumship sessions — your own quiet heart is already doing the work of continuing bonds beautifully.

dream-about-deceased-loved-one.title: What Is Your Grief Dream Surfacing?
dream-about-deceased-loved-one.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. It maps the structure of your dream, how it aligns with your grief stage, and what internal resolution it is pointing toward.
dream-about-deceased-loved-one.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads whether your dream is serving emotional resolution, memory integration, or trauma replay, and matches you with a grounded next step.

questions.q: When did your loved one pass away?
questions.hint: Dream architecture changes dramatically as bereavement matures.

questions.q: How did they look and appear in your dream?
questions.hint: The physical state in the dream reflects where your memory is anchored.

questions.q: What was the overall tone of communication and feeling?
questions.hint: What was the emotional atmosphere of the dream?

questions.q: How did you feel the morning after waking from the dream?
questions.hint: The waking afterglow is the truest marker of the dream’s psychological function.

questions.q: How often do you have dreams of this nature?
questions.hint: Milestone dreams heal; chronic dream loops signal emotional trauma.

questions.q: Were there unresolved conflicts or unspoken words between you when they died?
questions.hint: Subconscious dreams frequently work through relational debris.

questions.q: What are you most hoping this dream represents?
questions.hint: Your hope reveals the underlying need.

questions.q: What kind of clarity would be most helpful right now?
questions.hint: What supports your emotional balance?

patternDetails.summary: A profound milestone dream that provided genuine emotional peace and closure.
patternDetails.dontTell: It cannot be certified by third-party instruments — but you do not need outside verification to accept the peace it gave you.

patternDetails.summary: Your dream is replaying the shock of death, reflecting waking post-traumatic stress.
patternDetails.dontTell: It is not an omen of bad luck or proof that their soul is restless — it is post-traumatic stress in your own nervous system.

patternDetails.summary: The dream was tense or silent, reflecting your own unexpressed regrets and longing for absolution.
patternDetails.dontTell: Their dream figure is not holding a grudge — the harshness in the dream is your own guilt wearing their face.

patternDetails.summary: Everyday dreams reflecting the brain updating its reality map to incorporate their absence.
patternDetails.dontTell: It does not mean you are failing to move on — the brain takes months or years to rewire lifelong habits of presence.

patternDetails.summary: Fragmented dream elements that need time before their emotional meaning becomes clear.
patternDetails.dontTell: You do not need to rush to a dream dictionary — generic symbols rarely capture the truth of personal bereavement.

is-my-loved-one-watching-over-me.title: What Is Your Need for Reassurance Asking For?
is-my-loved-one-watching-over-me.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. It maps whether your relationship to their memory is providing a secure foundation or sustaining anxious loops, and maps the next step that fits.
is-my-loved-one-watching-over-me.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads whether wondering if they are watching is bringing comfort or creating decision paralysis, and matches you with a grounded next step.

questions.q: When does the question “are they watching over me” hit you hardest?
questions.hint: Context surfaces what the emotional need is.

questions.q: When you sit quietly and think of them, can you hear or imagine their advice?
questions.hint: Internalized neural models of loved ones are deeply accurate.

questions.q: How often do you seek external signs or psychic readings to confirm their presence?
questions.hint: Reassurance seeking can become an addictive substitute for self-trust.

questions.q: How does the thought of their gaze affect your big life choices?
questions.hint: Honoring memory vs. living in an imaginary prison.

questions.q: How does it feel when you go through long periods without “feeling” them near?
questions.hint: Does silence feel safe, or like abandonment?

questions.q: Do you ever feel guilty about experiencing joy, laughing, or thriving without them?
questions.hint: Survivor joy is often the hardest hurdle in grief.

questions.q: What are you most hoping an answer to this question will give you?
questions.hint: Name the real hunger.

questions.q: What kind of support would most stabilize you right now?
questions.hint: Match support to your emotional state.

patternDetails.summary: You carry their love as an internal compass that fosters courage rather than dependency.
patternDetails.dontTell: It does not prove metaphysical surveillance — but living with their internalized wisdom is far more valuable and real than chasing external signs.

patternDetails.summary: Wondering if they are watching has become an anxious cycle of seeking external approval.
patternDetails.dontTell: More psychic readings cannot soothe this loop — external reassurance wears off in days because the doubt lives in your own self-trust.

patternDetails.summary: You are delaying major life choices out of fear of betraying or disappointing their memory.
patternDetails.dontTell: Sacrificing your future does not honor their past — true love wants the surviving person to be safe, supported, and happy.

patternDetails.summary: Feeling only a painful void, leaving you exhausted and doubting the bond.
patternDetails.dontTell: The void does not mean the bond is dead — it means your brain is emotionally depleted and fighting for basic survival.

patternDetails.summary: Your relationship with their memory is evolving, with shifting moments of clarity and doubt.
patternDetails.dontTell: You do not need to rush to a fixed conclusion — continuing bonds take years to settle into a comfortable rhythm.

why-am-i-always-broke.title: What Is Driving Your Financial Cycle?
why-am-i-always-broke.subtitle: Eight questions, about two minutes. It sorts your financial friction into mathematical deficits, avoidance loops, boundary leakage, or emotional spending, and matches you with a realistic next step.
why-am-i-always-broke.launchSub: Eight questions, about two minutes. It reads whether your financial depletion is mathematical, behavioral, or boundary-related, and ends on the next step that fits.

questions.q: How does your net take-home income compare to your bare survival costs (rent, food, transit, minimum debt)?
questions.hint: Math first — you cannot budget your way out of a mathematical deficit.

questions.q: Where does the money seem to go when it disappears?
questions.hint: Identify the primary exit channel.

questions.q: How do you feel when you have to open your banking app or look at bills?
questions.hint: Money Avoidance script diagnosis.

questions.q: When are you most likely to spend money you know you should save?
questions.hint: Dopamine compensation triggers.

questions.q: How comfortable are you saying “no, I can’t afford that” to friends or family?
questions.hint: Boundary leakage is one of the most common causes of chronic broke-ness.

questions.q: What message about money did you absorb growing up?
questions.hint: Unconscious childhood money scripts run adult bank accounts.
